verdict.rationale: Statsig documents the programmatic write path an agent needs. The Console API is a CRUD API covering console actions, and the CLI can create, update and delete gates and configs, including from CI/CD. An official MCP server also exists, though its documented scope is asking questions and exploring data. The governance half of the story has no evidence: nothing shows approval workflows, required reviews, or any way to force agent-made flag changes through review before reaching production. Missing for 10: approval/review workflows gating flag changes, evidence that the MCP server can create or toggle flags, and per-token permission scoping to prevent unreviewed production writes.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: The Console API is the CRUD API for performing the actions available on console.statsig.com without using the web UI.
Create, update, and delete configs through commands, run them in scripts, or integrate Statsig configuration into CI/CD pipelines.
The Statsig CLI is a command-line interface that helps manage Feature Gates, Experiments, and Dynamic Configs within the Statsig platform.
The Statsig MCP (Model Context Protocol) server brings the power of Statsig into tools like Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code.
